academicChallenges: The current programme and course entries establish the neutral broad Biology route over Bioinformatics. All 21 first-year modules total 60 EC. Seven compulsory second-year modules total 30 EC; the official restricted Biology profiling group supplies another 30 EC. Final-year open study is 30 EC, methods and academic skills are 1+2+3 EC, and one research project is 24 EC. The 34 displayed components total 180 EC without double-counting both research-project options or including retired/noncurricular modules. Fresh Statistics 2 reports 3 EC, resolving the previous 4-EC mismatch. The historical 2025 OER is not needed to override the current catalogue.

The 30-EC restricted Biology group is real profiling space, with five teaching blocks and one available option per block. It remains explicitly restricted and distinct from final-year free study. Under Production Instructions 2.1, genuine profiling space can be preserved without inventing contents. The old seven-course bundle was not verified against its block constraints and is no longer asserted. Biology is the instantiated formal route; retaining its student-chosen profiling space neither substitutes a narrower UCR-friendly route nor claims a particular unverified course combination. Named options remain possibilities, not compulsory additions. There is no missing credit allocation or invented filler.

The project source expressly requires all first-year courses to be passed, normally runs 1 March–2 July 2027 for 90 full-time working days and requires an individual English report, even where students work in pairs. Normal biological/affiliated institutes and external-project approval are accurately distinguished. Statistics 2 normally runs in February before the project; General Research Skills assignments run during it. September participation/project starts require an approved adjusted plan. The nominal preceding years permit these conditions; current evidence establishes the pathway without a redundant unresolved OER requirement.

All 60 exact-target interest rows retain 16 generator-eligible, 28 supporting, eight illustrative and eight outcome roles. The broad closest response covers six eligible core rows; molecular/cellular and ecology/environment clusters account for the other eligible rows. Official Biology/Bioinformatics structure and current compulsory/elective content substantiate the directions. Illustrations and later careers do not generate programmes or establish UCR specialisations.

All three alternatives implement defining biological substance, rather than generic coherent methods: cell and molecular mechanisms, genetics, physiology, experimental/laboratory inquiry and disease or organismal/ecological systems. Broad and ecology routes include actual biodiversity, evolution, conservation, ecosystem and marine biology. The molecular route has a sustained cellular/biomedical core with neural-system applications and technical data methods. Ecology is strengthened by biochemistry/genetics, empirical statistics and numerical modelling. Earth/soil chemistry, climate and governance are specific complements to habitat conditions, environmental pressures and conservation decisions. Removing psycholinguistics, geohazards, an unavailable generic delta project and less direct materials physics improves those connections without relabelling them as biology.

Three current 24-course schedules each total 180 EC with four courses per term, Year-1 PPD and at least six advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite and actual assigned-term offering passes the workbook validator. Ecology places its biological gateway before physiology; Sustainability Essentials I precedes Environmental Biogeochemistry. Numerical methods follows Mathematical Methods. Neural networks is moved to its spring 2029 offering. Introductory data analysis precedes machine learning in the molecular route; statistics and machine learning can run concurrently where no formal prerequisite forbids it. Description-only courses receive their full supported contribution. Pairwise differences are 7 courses/52.5 EC, 5 courses/37.5 EC and 12 courses/90 EC in each direction, reflecting real biomedical versus environmental priorities.

All 34 placements were reconsidered against underlying content: 17 partial relations and 17 meaningful blanks. Source-first comparison established that enzymes, energy conversion and metabolism make Cell Physiology the stronger Biochemistry counterpart; Chemistry of Life is now a separate general-chemistry gap. Molecular Cell Biology shares replication/expression/regulation with molecular genetics, while Molecular Pathology and Genetics shares inheritance with Basic Genetics. Laboratory formation, organismal physiology, microbial immunity, mathematical/dynamic modelling and statistical methods are accurately partial. Marine Biology’s substantial public-outreach project supports the science-communication educational function without claiming the whole dedicated communication syllabus. Conservation aligns with applied Environmental Biology; the separate introductory Ecology requirement remains blank after the strongest modelling course is placed at Population and Community Ecology. Plant diversity, development, systems biology and bioethics remain legitimate gaps. No forced symmetry or misleading note about a nonexistent counterpart remains. Optional 15-EC independent research sits beside the required 24-EC project, outside scheduled 24 courses/180 EC.
